text:
Tom (Acme Ops): Hey team — after the cert rotation this morning (~04:00 UTC) our on‑prem SDKs in customer VPC are intermittently failing TLS verify. Seeing CRL fetch errors in our device logs. Filed a ticket but wanted to ping here since it's blocking traffic.

Anna (Support): Thanks Tom. Can you paste a small log snippet and the failing error? Also which Private region/VPC is this?

Tom (Acme Ops): VPC: eu-west-1-private. Error from our agent: 

```
2026-03-16T04:12:03Z agent TLS verify failed: certificate revoked? fetch CRL timed out (connect timeout)
at net/http.(*Client).Do ... verify.go:87
```

We run in FIPS mode so our stack checks CRLs, not OCSP. Our firewall only allows outbound to a small allowlist of IPs.

Anna (Support): Got it. Can you run a curl from a node inside the VPC to the CRL URL in the cert (or share the CRL URL)? Also confirm whether the SDK sees the new cert chain (fullchain) after rotation.

Tom (Acme Ops): CRL URL from the cert: `https://crl-pub.acme-certs.example/issuerA.crl`
Curl from a node: 

```
curl -v https://crl-pub.acme-certs.example/issuerA.crl --connect-timeout 5 -o /tmp/issuerA.crl
* About to connect() to crl-pub.acme-certs.example port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 198.51.100.23... connected.
* Connected to crl-pub.acme-certs.example (198.51.100.23) port 443 (#0)
> GET /issuerA.crl HTTP/1.1
> Host: crl-pub.acme-certs.example
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
... saved to /tmp/issuerA.crl
```

Then a second attempt returned a timeout: 
```
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5000 milliseconds with 0 out of 0 bytes received
```

So it's flaky.

Jake (Eng): Hmm — that CRL host is behind a CDN + dynamic egress pool. If your firewall allowlist is IP‑based, you'll see intermittent success when the CDN edge IP matches one of your allowed IPs. With CRLs we need reliable fetch for the cert revocation check.

Maria (SRE): Also, can you confirm the rotator actually published the new CRL with an updated serial after rotation? If the CRL wasn't updated, some clients might treat it as stale.

rotator-bot: rotation job id r-1942 finished: leaf and chain updated at 2026-03-16T03:58:47Z. CRL publish step: queued -> success (push to crl-pub.acme-certs.example).

Anna (Support): Tom, can you run `openssl crl -in /tmp/issuerA.crl -noout -text` and paste the `CRL Number` and `Last Update` fields?

Tom (Acme Ops): Ran it, got: 
```
$ openssl crl -in /tmp/issuerA.crl -noout -text
CRL Number: 0
Last Update: Mar 15 03:58:00 2026 GMT
Next Update: Mar 22 03:58:00 2026 GMT
```

Looks like CRL Number didn't increment (still 0) even though rotator reported publish success.

Jake (Eng): That's suspicious. Rotator reported success but serial didn't increment — likely the publish step pushed the same file or there was a write race. Two hypotheses: (1) CRL generation step failed but publisher returned 200 on PUT (edge CDN cached old file), or (2) your firewall caching + CDN TTL means clients hit an edge with stale copy.

Maria (SRE): Can you also capture the agent's HTTP error when it times out? We want to confirm it's actually connect timeouts to the CRL host, not a TLS handshake after connect.

Tom (Acme Ops): Here's a failing agent trace: 
```
2026-03-16T04:12:03Z CRL fetch https://crl-pub.acme-certs.example/issuerA.crl failed: dial tcp 198.51.100.45:443: i/o timeout
```

That ip 198.51.100.45 isn't in our allowlist; allowlist currently has 198.51.100.23 and 198.51.100.67.

Anna (Support): OK — this matches the CDN/dynamic IP theory. Short term we can suggest adding the CRL hostname to your firewall allowlist (SNI/domain allow) or expand the IP range to include CDN edges. Long term we should avoid relying on IP allowlists for CRL/OCSP endpoints.

Jake (Eng): Also, we need to re-publish the CRL with an incremented CRL number to ensure no stale clients treat the file as unchanged. I'll trigger a manual re-publish and flush cache. @rotator-bot can you re-run `publish-crl --force r-1942`?

rotator-bot: publish-crl --force r-1942 -> started
rotator-bot: publish-crl --force r-1942 -> success (pushed new CRL, crl number 3, Last Update: 2026-03-16T04:35:10Z)

Tom (Acme Ops): After re-publish I retried curl from the node a few times: sometimes 200, sometimes timeout.

Maria (SRE): That still suggests the firewall drop is the root cause. Can you ask your network team to temporarily allow the hostname (TLS SNI) or add the CDN ASN / broader IP blocks for `crl-pub.acme-certs.example`? Also restart the agent to clear any in-memory cache so it fetches the new CRL.

Tom (Acme Ops): Network team added SNI allow rule: `crl-pub.acme-certs.example`. Restarted agent. Now agent logs: 
```
2026-03-16T04:40:12Z CRL fetch https://crl-pub.acme-certs.example/issuerA.crl succeeded, CRL Number: 3
2026-03-16T04:40:12Z TLS verify passed, connection established
```

Looks stable after the SNI allow. 👍

Anna (Support): Great. Root cause summary: edge CDN for CRL host uses dynamic IPs; VPC firewall was IP‑only allowlist causing intermittent CRL fetch timeouts. Also rotator published a new CRL but the initial publish may have hit CDN cache / not incremented (CRL Number 0) — we forced a re-publish with incremented CRL number and requested cache flush.

Jake (Eng): Action items: (1) Engineering to add explicit cache flush on CRL publish (tracking ticket INF-3284), (2) Recommend customers use domain/SNI‑based egress allowlisting for CRL/OCSP endpoints or whitelist CDN ASN ranges, (3) We'll add a rotator health check to verify CRL Number increments post-publish.

Maria (SRE): I'll create the infra ticket and link here. Also recommend docs update for Private customers about CRL/OCSP egress guidance.

Tom (Acme Ops): Thanks all — confirmed the client fleet recovered after the SNI allow and agent restart. Please let us know when INF-3284 is done so we can close the internal change.

Anna (Support): Marking this thread as resolved for now. If you see any regression, ping us and we'll reopen. :thumbsup:
